universal_lens: The instep kick is formalized as a time-frequency operator acting on a multi-channel sEMG Hilbert space. Skill-level divergence emerges not from global amplitude scaling, but from phase-specific spectral redistribution, mathematically captured by the localized eigen-trajectories of a Morlet-wavelet transformed covariance matrix.
gsi_mapping: GSI maps the normalized kicking timeline to a conformal prediction interval. The significant PC3 and PC1 score divergences act as high-dimensional features; Bayesian updating quantifies the posterior probability that an observed time-frequency intensity map originates from an elite neuromuscular control distribution versus an amateur baseline.
gse_mapping: GSE models the kick as a state-transition system across Phase 1 (acceleration) and Phase 2 (follow-through). Elite states are defined by mid-frequency biceps femoris dominance, while amateur states exhibit higher-frequency medial gastrocnemius reliance, allowing real-time situational reasoning about joint stability and limb deceleration.

reasoning_traces.think:
The mathematical derivation begins by treating the seven-channel sEMG recording as a multivariate stochastic process X(t). We apply a biphasic temporal partitioning operator P, splitting the domain into pre-contact (Phase 1) and post-contact (Phase 2) intervals based on kinematic singularities. Within these intervals, we apply a continuous Morlet wavelet transform W to project X(t) into a time-frequency intensity manifold M(t,f). This transformation captures both transient bursts and sustained activations, moving beyond simple RMS amplitude metrics. To reduce dimensionality while preserving maximal variance, Global Principal Component Analysis (GPCA) is applied to the concatenated spectral features, yielding orthogonal modes PC1 through PC6. The core duality emerges in the statistical evaluation of these modes: SPM1D t-tests reveal that skill-level differences are not global scalings but highly localized perturbations in the PC score trajectories. Specifically, PC3 diverges significantly in Phase 1 (54-75%), driven by mid-frequency biceps femoris activity, while PC1 diverges in Phase 2 (60-70%), driven by high-frequency medial gastrocnemius reliance in amateurs. The failure mode of this framework lies in its reliance on linear decomposition; if elite coordination relies on highly non-linear, chaotic cross-muscle coupling, the first six PCs might fail to capture the true invariant subspace of expert performance.

reasoning_traces.retrocausal_genealogy: This analytical pipeline inherits from the foundational work of Daubechies on wavelet transforms for non-stationary biological signals, merged with spatial statistics pioneered by Kieffer and Pataky in SPM1D. Historically, biomechanics relied on static RMS comparisons; the shift to time-frequency PCA reflects a broader mathematical migration toward functional data analysis, treating movement not as discrete points but as continuous curves in a high-dimensional Hilbert space.
reasoning_traces.theory_of_mind: We model two opposing decision actors: the Elite Controller and the Amateur Controller. The Elite Controller optimizes for kinetic chain efficiency, utilizing the biceps femoris as a precise, mid-frequency brake to stabilize the knee immediately prior to impact. Conversely, the Amateur Controller, lacking proximal control, exhibits a reactive strategy, relying heavily on distal, high-frequency medial gastrocnemius bursts to compensate for instability during the chaotic post-contact follow-through. The primitives quantify this strategic divergence.
reasoning_traces.cross_layer_veto: To prevent anti-collinearity and leakage between layers, we strictly veto any interpretation that conflates EMG amplitude with mechanical force output. The spectral kernels must remain purely descriptive of neural drive timing and frequency content.
